Extraversive incorporative to ok'om (óol). It is ambiguous between an extraversive ("sadden"/"traurig stimmen") and a causative ("mourn"/"betrauern") reading.
The lemma might as well be ok'om óol, as the latter component is obligatory.

This is an irregluar verb where neither the intransitive nor the transitive version are clearly basic. Here the intransitive stem will be taken as basic.

Relational adjectival experiential construction: [ [ W ]Adj -Absi [ ti' [ PossE Li [ E ]NP ]NP ]PrepP [ S ]NPi ]S; "S is W to E's X", where L is a body part sensu lato of E. This is an expansion of the relational adjectival predicate construction. This construction follows a pattern, but is lexicalized. Since the base is adjectival, there are no valency alternations.

"load on oneself". Consequently, L is normally not specified, but may be incorporated, as in #333. There is no basic verb for loading things anywhere else. The semantically closest derived verb is na'ks 'move up'.
Variant k'oha'nkunt. Factitive of k'oha'n. The variant k'oha'nkuns has the causative instead of the extraversive suffix.
factitive to kah. kahkuns and kahbes are causative variants.
This is the (extraversive) verbalization of the noun sóol 'shell, bark', which is, thus, lexically implicit.
uncoded alternation ! The version with P as direct object appears to be basic.
German 'schubsen'. The verb is composed of the verbal roots len 'stick' and ch'in 'pelt'.
The verb means both 'give' and 'put'. It is the basic trivalent verb of the language.

regular causative of balak'. The stem balak't is formally extraversive, but semantically a variant of the causative.

extraversive to ookol. ookolt displays an uncoded alternation of assigning direct object function either to the stolen thing or to the robbed person. As it is the only verb, besides púust, to do so, no alternation was set up.

Causative of the passive ka'n of kan 'learn'.- ka'ns displays an uncoded alternation concerning the assignment of direct and indirect object to the two oblique arguments. As it is the only verb to do so, no alternation was set up.

'pelt'. Does not fit the intended role frame.

There is no base verb meaning 'touch' in Maya. mach 'seize' is the semantically closest root. Semantically closer stems are compounds. See also koh. Mach appears in the instrumental frame only exceptionally (ex. 334), as the use of hands is part of its meaning.
isíint, as in 139, is a morphological variant (extraversive instead of causative transitivization).
There is suppletion between isíin (tr.) and ichkíil (intr.).
ichíint [X]obj [Y]subj means 'Y uses X for washing, Y washes with X'
The basic meaning is apparently 'to free X from dirt by shaking'. No instrument specifiable.
